passages.text: # How I Built a $1M Solo AI Business... Then Rebuilt It
*TLDR… I launched Blotato by using AI to test demand, vibe code my first version, build distribution through content, survive a messy failure-prone launch, then rebuild once I had conviction.*
## 1. The Idea Was A Public Question

The comments told me the pain was real enough to try building it. Very honestly, I figured if Blotato flopped, I could just release the code as open-source and make content out of it! That’s why it felt low-risk and not that serious.
## 2. The Vision Was Too Big, So I Cut It Down
On August 4, 2024, I filmed myself building the MVP in a 7-part Youtube series using Cursor AI. This was before Cursor Composer - I literally had to CREATE and DELETE files manually.
Original Blotato vision Google Doc and Spec V1 from August 2 2024 showing AI-powered remixing and the first SaaS app spec
So I drew the first UX prototype with URL input, text input, LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, images, edit buttons, and publish buttons.
Final Blotato v1 UX prototype after stripping non-essential features down to text input, Facebook selection, submit, and one output card
Gross looking Cursor-built Blotato MVP running locally with a Content Repurposer create screen, Facebook output, Edit Prompt button, and Publish button
## 3. Early Adopters Proved Interest Is Not The Same As Behavior
It promised the first 50 early adopters a steep lifetime discount and personal, priority support from me, the founder.
I uploaded the wrong video, linked it in the newsletter, sent it to thousands of people, then made the video private!
